name: one min variable breaks on pop
hook: Keep a stack's minimum in one variable. It works until you pop the minimum.
hook_slide: One `min` variable works. *Until you pop the minimum.*
hook_sub: A stack that answers getMin in O(1), and the version that almost does.
caption: Design a stack with push, pop, top and getMin, all in O(1). The obvious version keeps a single min variable and updates it on every push.

Push -2, 0, -3 and getMin says -3. Pop, and the stack holds {left}. The variable still says {one_min_says}, a value that is gone. The new minimum is whatever was minimal before it arrived, and one overwritten variable has destroyed that.
The patch is to rescan the stack on every getMin: {scan_reads} elements read to empty a stack of {n}, asking for the minimum before each pop.
The fix: pops undo pushes in exact reverse order, so snapshot the minimum alongside each push, on a second stack. Pop discards exactly the snapshot that expires. Same {n} values: {snap_reads} reads.
State that unwinds with the stack lives on a stack. Where else have you seen that? 👇
